finding: The existing shared Finno-Ugric naming key does not validate Lithuanian, Latvian, Prussian, Estonian and Finnish inventories.
decision: Use targeted_name_corpora.json. Finnish/Lithuanian pools and bounded Latvian/Estonian female selections are supplied. Old Prussian masculine core is supplied; no new feminine default is authorised. Do not delegate invention or silently use a neighbouring pool.

finding: A Western Slavic fallback is not an adequate Romanian repertoire.
decision: Use 28 masculine and 17 feminine groups with per-entry era scope; dynastic and inscription provenance is explicit. Equal gameplay weights, no claim of representative commoner frequencies.

scope: Coptic and Syriac Christian name profiles
finding: Arabic political-template profiles can contain an inappropriate religious repertoire.
decision: Use separate Coptic and Syriac pools. Preserve the distinction between documentary names and devotional/literary repertoire. No claim that a saint floruit dates a vernacular spelling or represents ordinary-name frequencies.

finding: Existing morphology must survive consolidation; a surname ending is not a universally productive rule.
decision: No new productive gender morphology. Reuse reviewed atomic names, optional bynames and existing proven forms. Run naming_pattern_tests.json through actual parser/renderer. No adopted-name selector.

finding: Greek, English and Persian may denote different stages in different source modules.
decision: Bind by source context and canonical stage. Do not upsert based on label equality alone.

scope: Circassian, Avestan and ancient Egyptian elective dependencies
finding: Those retained-catalogue candidate names are not newly specified language records here.
decision: Resolve an actual suitable record or leave the optional candidate visibly unimplemented; never pretend an unrelated language is equivalent.

finding: Era toolkits deliberately overlap and contain material from different centuries.
decision: Retain applicability notes, regional variants and title changes; do not invent a single date of peoplehood emergence.

finding: Unsupported non-decomposing letters become question marks, and the fallback buffer is shared.
decision: Implement the supplied map/NFC/isolation policy; verify the actual .NET encoder and chargen round-trip before enabling new unsupported source spellings.

scope: Generic skill-group dependency and profile preservation
finding: PR730 implements the generic feature. Original profile upserts still need non-destructive reconciliation in this CultureSeeder work.
decision: Use ChargenSkillSelectionGroupSeeder.Upsert; do not rebuild groups, screens or allocator. Preserve names and builder edits through the separately specified source/baseline ledger.
